answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers aggregate penalties that scale as O(k²), not merely linearly. Detection also applies asymmetric capital depreciation: a swarm’s correlated violations compound into an exponential multiplier in capital loss, making the apparent advantage of splitting control across identities costly. A thread of evidence can expose the gale of coordination, while karst-like collateral locks keep bonds unavailable for escape.
